punchline: Same ancestry, 38% versus 6.9% diabetes: the difference was the place.
thirty_sec: A 2006 Diabetes Care study compared Pima in Arizona and in Mexico. Age- and sex-adjusted type 2 diabetes was about 38% in Arizona, 6.9% in Mexico, close to the 2.6% of non-Pima Mexicans. The groups are genetically similar, so the authors blamed Westernized lifestyle.
question: Where do you explain a difference by who people are when it may be where they are?
key_contrast: Similar genes, very different diabetes rates; the setting differed.
